804.headline: A close look at the prizes

805.body:
"Multiply Your Money" is near the midpoint of its run, with about half of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

The numbers for "Multiply Your Money" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.

The key fact about "Extreme Green" is how its eleven prize levels are built. The prize money leans toward small, frequent prizes. Games built like this pay small prizes often and large prizes rarely. Prize counts change daily, but this design does not.

812.body:
"Loose Change®" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $1,000 was claimed in today's numbers. Unsold tickets still hold eighteen of the original 24. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

812.headline: Another top prize was claimed

813.body:
"The Price is Right™" has gone two weeks without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About a quarter of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $50,000 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

If "The Price is Right™" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
